## Fact check (new laws and rulings)

Status: HOLD

Two of the post's three central claims are problematic: the SMS 'overhaul' the post treats as a completed 2026 reality has not yet gone live as of late October 2026 (the old seven-BASIC methodology is still in effect), and the claim that 2026 rules impose a broker duty to verify carrier safety scores is not supported — the actual 2026 broker rule addresses financial responsibility and identity proofing, not safety-score vetting obligations. The electronic medical certification transition is real and accurately described, though it took effect in 2025 (not 2026), with full paper-waiver expiration in October 2026.

- Confirmed: Starting in 2025 and fully implemented through 2026, FMCSA moved to a fully electronic medical certification system tied directly to the CDL database, replacing the old paper-based system.
  - Source: https://sambasafety.com/blog/new-fmcsa-electronic-medical-certification-reporting-under-nrii
- Confirmed: Medical examiners now submit driver medical exam results directly to FMCSA's National Registry electronically, with a timestamp, and results link automatically to the driver's CDL record at the state level.
  - Source: https://gomotive.com/blog/fmcsas-digital-shift-for-modernized-medical-certification/
- REVIEW: fact check CONTRADICTED: The rebuilt Safety Measurement System (SMS) more accurately reflects a carrier's actual safety history, with the 2026 overhaul having been completed and now in effect. (As of October 20, 2026, FMCSA's enhanced SMS methodology has not launched — every carrier's SMS results still use the old method (version 3.21, revised May 2026) and FMCSA has published no launch date for the new scoring system.)
  - Source: https://lucideld.com/news/fmcsa-csa-changes-2026
- Confirmed: The post describes the SMS as still scoring carriers on seven categories (unsafe driving, hours-of-service compliance, driver fitness, controlled substances and alcohol, vehicle maintenance, hazardous materials compliance, and crash history).
  - Source: https://lucideld.com/news/fmcsa-csa-changes-2026
- REVIEW: fact check CONTRADICTED: 2026 federal rules require brokers to verify carrier safety scores and insurance before placing loads, creating a documented vetting obligation. (The 2026 FMCSA Broker and Freight Forwarder Financial Responsibility Rule (effective January 16, 2026) addresses financial security and identity proofing, not a mandate to verify carrier SMS safety scores; a pending congressional bill (S. 5337) that would create a carrier safety-vetting obligation for brokers has not advanced since September 2025, and a Supreme Court source confirms FMCSA imposes no safety standard on broker hiring beyond using a registered carrier.)
  - Source: https://simplexgroup.net/supreme-court-expands-freight-broker-liability/
